draft.title: Genghis Khan unites the Mongols
card: The Mongols were nomadic herders of the Central Asian steppe. They lived in separate tribes, and the tribes often fought each other.
A leader named Temujin won power over rival tribes through alliances and war. In 1206 the Mongol chiefs met and gave him the title Genghis Khan, which is often translated as universal ruler.
Before this, leaders usually gave the top jobs to relatives and men from their own clan. Genghis Khan promoted followers for loyalty and skill instead, whatever family they came from.
This rewarded able people and tied them to him. Many tribes became one Mongol nation with one leader.
draft.remember: Genghis Khan joined the tribes by rewarding loyalty and skill, not birth.

a.q: How did Genghis Khan choose many of his commanders and officials?
opts: By loyalty and skill, whatever their family
By which clan they were born into
By how much land their families owned
By how long their families had led a tribe
a.why: He promoted people who were loyal and able, even if they came from humble families. Choosing by clan was the older custom he moved away from.
a.clue: Think about what he valued more than family.

b.q: Two Mongol men serve Genghis Khan. Borte comes from a leading clan but is often disloyal. Subutai comes from a humble family but is loyal and a gifted soldier. Who is more likely to be promoted?
opts: Subutai, because he is loyal and skilled
Borte, because he comes from a leading clan
Borte, because leaders gave top jobs to relatives
Neither, because tribes chose all the commanders
b.why: Genghis Khan promoted on loyalty and skill, and Subutai has both. Borte's clan would have helped under the older custom, but it did not decide promotion for Genghis Khan.
b.clue: Which man has the qualities Genghis Khan rewarded?

a.best: By loyalty and skill, whatever their family

b.best: Subutai, because he is loyal and skilled

problems.detail: Borte (Börte) was Genghis Khan's wife. Using the name for a disloyal Mongol man is historically misleading, and could confuse students who later meet her. Use an invented or generic name instead.
The clue 'Think about what he valued more than family' gives the answer away. Every distractor is about family, so only the right option fits the clue.
The right option is the only one that is not about family, and it carries the extra qualifier 'whatever their family'. It stands out from the three family-based distractors.

The remember line says he joined the tribes by rewarding loyalty and skill. The card says he won power through alliances and war, and that promotion by merit then bound followers to him. The line oversimplifies how the tribes were united.
